Captain America is a fictional superhero appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics. The character was created by Joe Simon and Jack Kirby and first appeared in Captain America Comics #1 in March 1941.

The original character, Steve Rogers, was a frail young man who was deemed unfit for military service during World War II. He volunteered for a top-secret research project, known as the Super Soldier program, which aimed to create a new breed of soldiers. Rogers was injected with a serum that turned him into a physically perfect human being, and he was given a red, white, and blue costume and a shield made of vibranium, a rare metal.

As Captain America, Rogers fought against the Axis powers during World War II, becoming a symbol of American patriotism and courage. He was a member of the superhero team the Avengers and has continued to fight against various villains and threats to the world.

In the comics, Captain America has been portrayed as a man out of time, having been frozen in ice for decades and waking up in the present day. This has allowed writers to explore themes of patriotism, duty, and the struggle to adapt to changing times.

Captain America has been adapted into various forms of media, including movies, TV shows, and video games. He has become one of Marvel's most iconic and recognizable characters, and his shield has become a symbol of heroism and American values.
